india.name: Shelf life left at delivery (online sales)
india.citation: FSSAI advisory to e-commerce food businesses, Nov 2024: at least 30% of shelf life or 45 days before expiry at delivery

source.label: FSSAI advisory, reported by All India Radio (NewsOnAir)

india.explanation: Food sold online in India must reach the customer with at least 30% of its shelf life, or 45 days, left before expiry. This depends on your stock rotation, not the label.
india.advice: Plan dispatch so every order arrives with at least 30% of shelf life or 45 days left.

rules.name: Blood sugar or diabetes wording
rules.citation: Amazon policy on diabetes-related products (products marketed as diabetes, glucose or sugar treatments need FDA approval), as quoted in a Seller Central forum thread; compliance guides report automated review treats "blood sugar" as a high-sensitivity term
rules.explanation: Amazon's automated review flags blood-sugar, glucose and diabetes wording on food and supplement listings, even when the FDA would accept it as a structure/function claim.
rules.advice: For Amazon, remove this sentence, or keep qualified wording ("…blood sugar levels already within a normal range") and have documentation ready for an appeal.

rules.name: Shelf life too short for Amazon.in
rules.citation: Amazon.in Grocery & Gourmet Foods Listing Policy: minimum shelf life of 3 months (seller-fulfilled) or 5 months (Fulfilled by Amazon)

source.label: Amazon.in Grocery & Gourmet Foods Listing Policy (PDF)

rules.explanation: Amazon.in needs food products to have at least 3 months of shelf life (5 months if Fulfilled by Amazon).
rules.advice: Extend the shelf life to at least 3 months (5 for FBA), or sell this product through a channel with a shorter minimum.

rules.name: FSSAI licence valid 2+ months, covering this category
rules.citation: Amazon.in Grocery & Gourmet Foods Listing Policy: FSSAI licence valid for at least 2 months ahead, with a scope that covers the products listed

source.label: Amazon.in Grocery & Gourmet Foods Listing Policy (PDF)

rules.explanation: Amazon.in removes listings if the FSSAI licence expires within 2 months or doesn't cover the product category.
rules.advice: Check your licence's expiry date and scope before listing.

rules.name: Shelf life too short for Blinkit
rules.citation: Third-party onboarding guides report Blinkit wants 90 to 120 days of shelf life left at warehouse intake
rules.explanation: Blinkit is reported to need at least 90 days of shelf life left when stock arrives at its warehouse.
rules.advice: Confirm the current threshold with Blinkit; products with under 90 days of total shelf life are likely to be refused.

rules.name: FSSAI number printed on the pack, not a sticker
rules.citation: Third-party onboarding guides report Blinkit holds listings when the FSSAI number is only on a sticker or insert
rules.explanation: Blinkit is reported to check that the FSSAI number is printed on the primary pack, not added as a sticker or insert.
rules.advice: Print the FSSAI number on the primary pack.

rules.name: About 60% shelf life left at intake
rules.citation: Third-party onboarding guides report Zepto wants about 60% of total shelf life left at warehouse intake
rules.explanation: Zepto is reported to need about 60% of the product's total shelf life left when stock arrives. This depends on dispatch timing, not the label.
rules.advice: Plan dispatch so stock arrives with about 60% of its shelf life left; confirm the threshold with Zepto.

rules.name: GS1 (EAN) barcode on every unit
rules.citation: Third-party checklists report quick-commerce platforms need a GS1-based EAN barcode on each unit; internal codes and QR codes aren't accepted
rules.explanation: Zepto is reported to need a scannable GS1 (EAN) barcode on every unit.
rules.advice: Register with GS1 India and print the EAN barcode on each unit.

rules.name: About 60% shelf life left at intake
rules.citation: Third-party onboarding guides report Instamart wants about 60% of total shelf life left at warehouse intake; Instamart doesn't publish its requirements
rules.explanation: Instamart is reported to need about 60% of the product's total shelf life left when stock arrives.
rules.advice: Plan dispatch so stock arrives with about 60% of its shelf life left; confirm the threshold with Instamart.

rules.name: Shelf life too short (assumed Amazon.in policy)
rules.citation: No public Amazon Now policy found; assumed to follow the Amazon.in Grocery & Gourmet Foods Listing Policy (minimum 3 months of shelf life)

source.label: Amazon.in Grocery & Gourmet Foods Listing Policy (PDF)

rules.explanation: Amazon Now is assumed to follow Amazon.in's grocery policy, which needs at least 3 months of shelf life.
rules.advice: Confirm Amazon Now's shelf-life minimum with Amazon before listing.
